# Introduction

`LipidMS` is an R package for lipid annotation in LC-MS/MS-based
lipidomics experiments.

The current implementation of `LipidMS` works directly with
`XcmsExperiment` objects. This allows lipid annotation to be integrated into
standard Bioconductor mass spectrometry workflows without requiring
intermediate export of peak tables or MS/MS spectra.

An `XcmsExperiment` can contain, within the same object:

- sample metadata,
- MS1 and MS2 spectra,
- detected chromatographic peaks,
- retention-time information,
- grouped chromatographic features,
- and lipid annotations generated by `LipidMS`.

This organization keeps the relationship between raw spectra,
chromatographic peaks, features and lipid annotations throughout the complete
analysis.

The general workflow is:

```text
mzML files
    |
    v
MsExperiment
    |
    v
xcms processing
    |
    v
XcmsExperiment
    |
    v
LipidMS annotation
    |
    v
Annotated XcmsExperiment
```

# Complete LC-MS experiment

A typical LipidMS experiment can combine several acquisition modes.

For example, the following dataset contains six positive-ionization plasma
samples:

```text
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DDA_01.mzML
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DDA_02.mzML
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DIA_01.mzML
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DIA_02.mzML
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_MS_01.mzML
20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_MS_02.mzML
```

These files represent three acquisition strategies:

- **Full Scan**, providing MS1 information.
- **DDA**, providing MS1 and data-dependent MS2 spectra.
- **DIA**, providing MS1 and data-independent MS2 spectra.

The mzML files used in this example can be downloaded from:

```text
REPOSITORY_URL
```

The following sections show how a complete experiment can be constructed
from these files.

The mzML files are not processed when this vignette is built because doing
so would substantially increase package build time and would require access
to external files.

# Load packages

```{r libraries-full, eval=TRUE}
library(LipidMS)
library(xcms)
library(MsExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
```

# Import mzML files

First, define the files:

```{r files, eval=FALSE}
files <- file.path(
    "data",
    c(
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DDA_01.mzML",
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DDA_02.mzML",
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DIA_01.mzML",
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_DIA_02.mzML",
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_MS_01.mzML",
        "20250930_plasmaNIST_pos_MS_02.mzML"
    )
)
```

The acquisition mode of each sample is stored in the sample metadata:

```{r metadata-full, eval=FALSE}
sample_data <- DataFrame(
    sample = basename(files),
    acquisition_mode = c(
        "DDA",
        "DDA",
        "DIA",
        "DIA",
        "FULLSCAN",
        "FULLSCAN"
    ),
    row.names = basename(files)
)

sample_data
```

The raw LC-MS data can then be imported as an `MsExperiment`:

```{r import-full, eval=FALSE}
x <- readMsExperiment(
    files,
    sampleData = sample_data
)

x
```

# Chromatographic peak detection

Chromatographic peaks are detected using the any algorithm implemented
in `xcms`.

```{r peak-detection parameters, eval=TRUE}
cwp_ms1 <- CentWaveParam(
    ppm = 25,
    peakwidth = c(5, 50),
    snthresh = 10,
    prefilter = c(5, 100),
    mzCenterFun = "wMean",
    integrate = 2
)
```

```{r peak-detection, eval=FALSE}
x <- findChromPeaks(
    x,
    param = cwp_ms1
)
```


Peaks are initially grouped across samples:

```{r grouping-pre param, eval=TRUE}
grp_param <- PeakDensityParam(
        sampleGroups = rep(1, 6),
        bw = 5,
        minFraction = 0.9,
        binSize = 0.01
    )
```


```{r grouping-pre, eval=FALSE}
x <- groupChromPeaks(
    x,
    param = grp_param
)
```

# Retention-time correction

Retention times can be aligned using chromatographic peak groups:

```{r retention-time param, eval=TRUE}
rt_param <- PeakGroupsParam(
        minFraction = 0.9,
        extraPeaks = 1,
        smooth = "loess",
        span = 0.4,
        family = "gaussian"
    )
```


```{r retention-time, eval=FALSE}
x <- adjustRtime(
    x,
    param = rt_param
)
```

After retention-time correction, chromatographic peaks are grouped again:

```{r grouping post param, eval=TRUE}
grp_param_post <- PeakDensityParam(
        sampleGroups = rep(1, 6),
        bw = 5,
        minFraction = 0.5,
        binSize = 0.01
    )
```

```{r grouping post, eval=FALSE}
x <- groupChromPeaks(
    x,
    param = grp_param_post
)
```

Missing chromatographic peak intensities can then be integrated:

```{r fill peaks full, eval=FALSE}
x <- fillChromPeaks(
    x,
    param = ChromPeakAreaParam()
)
```

At this stage, the object contains the processed chromatographic experiment
that will be used by `LipidMS`.

```{r xcms results inspection, eval=FALSE}
head(featureDefinitions(x))
```

# LipidMS parameters for a complete experiment

LipidMS annotation parameters can be explicitly defined as follows:

```{r annotation parameters, eval=TRUE}
paramannot <- list(
    polarity = "positive",
    dmzprecursor = 10,
    dmzproducts = 15,
    rttol = 3,
    isotope_mzabs = 0.01,
    isotope_maxcharge = 2L,
    isotope_maxiso = 5L,
    isotope_minfrac = 0.5,
    isotope_rttol = 5,
    intval = "into",
    min_ms2_intensity = 100,
    remove_isotopes = TRUE
)
```

For experiments containing DIA samples, additional parameters define the
MS2 chromatographic peak extraction:

```{r dia parameters, eval=TRUE}
cwp_ms2 <- CentWaveParam(
    ppm = 25,
    peakwidth = c(3, 50),
    snthresh = 2,
    prefilter = c(3, 50),
    mzCenterFun = "wMean",
    integrate = 2,
    mzdiff = -0.001
)

paramdia <- list(
    findChromPeaksIsolationWindowParam = cwp_ms2,
    expandRt = 0,
    minCor = 0.7,
    diffRt = 3,
    intensity = "into",
    minint = 100,
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
```

The complete lipid annotation can then be performed with:

```{r annotation, eval=FALSE}
x <- annotateLipids(
    x,
    paramannot = paramannot,
    paramdia = paramdia,
    verbose = FALSE
)
```

`annotateLipids()` uses the acquisition mode stored in `sampleData(x)` to
determine which samples provide MS1 information and which samples can also
provide MS2 fragmentation evidence.


# Reproducible example included with LipidMS

The complete workflow above illustrates how LipidMS can be used starting from
multiple mzML files.

To provide a small and reproducible example that can also be evaluated when
the vignette is built, the package includes `xcmsexperiment_negative`.

This object was generated from a negative-ionization DDA plasma sample and
contains only a short retention-time interval. Chromatographic peak detection
and feature grouping have already been performed.

```{r libraries-example, eval = FALSE}
library(LipidMS)
library(xcms)
library(MsExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
```

Load the example object:

```{r load-example}
data("xcmsexperiment_negative", package = "LipidMS")

x <- xcmsexperiment_negative
```

The object is an `XcmsExperiment`:

```{r show-example}
x
```

The associated sample metadata contain the acquisition mode:

```{r sample-data-example}
sampleData(x)
```

Chromatographic peaks are already available:

```{r peaks-example}
head(chromPeaks(x))
```

Grouped chromatographic features can also be inspected:

```{r features-before-example}
head(featureDefinitions(x))
```

# Lipid annotation of the example data

The example was acquired in negative ionization mode, so the annotation
parameters are:

```{r annotation-parameters example}
paramannot <- list(
    polarity = "negative",
    dmzprecursor = 10,
    dmzproducts = 15,
    rttol = 3,
    isotope_mzabs = 0.01,
    isotope_maxcharge = 2L,
    isotope_maxiso = 5L,
    isotope_minfrac = 0.5,
    isotope_rttol = 5,
    intval = "into",
    min_ms2_intensity = 100,
    remove_isotopes = TRUE
)
```

The example contains DDA data only. Therefore, no DIA-specific extraction
parameters are required.

```{r annotation example}
x <- annotateLipids(
    x,
    paramannot = paramannot,
    paramdia = list(),
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
    verbose = FALSE
)
```

The complete LipidMS workflow is performed by `annotateLipids()`, including
MS1 candidate generation, isotope annotation, grouping of coeluting adducts,
MS2 extraction, fragmentation-rule matching and organization of the final
annotations.

# Annotation results

LipidMS stores annotation information directly inside the
`XcmsExperiment`.

Peak-level information is stored in `chromPeakData()`.

```{r peak-annotation-results}
peak_results <- chromPeakData(x)

head(
    peak_results[peak_results$has_lipid_ms2_annotation, c(
        "has_lipid_ms2_annotation",
        "lipid_class",
        "sum_composition",
        "annotation_level",
        "annotation"
    )]
)
```

Feature-level annotations are stored in `featureDefinitions()`.

```{r feature-annotation-results}
feature_results <- featureDefinitions(x)

head(
    feature_results[feature_results$has_lipid_ms2_annotation, c(
        "mzmed",
        "rtmed",
        "has_lipid_ms2_annotation",
        "lipid_class",
        "sum_composition",
        "annotation_level",
        "annotation"
    )]
)
```

Quantitative information remains accessible through the standard `xcms`
interface:

```{r feature-values-example}
head(
    featureValues(
        x,
        value = "into",
        filled = TRUE
    )
)
```

Thus, the same experiment object contains chromatographic information,
quantitative data and lipid annotations.

# LipidMS information stored in the experiment

LipidMS also stores auxiliary annotation information in the metadata of the
`XcmsExperiment`.

```{r lipidms-metadata}
names(S4Vectors::metadata(x)$LipidMS)
```

This allows annotation parameters and intermediate results to remain
associated with the processed experiment.

# Why use XcmsExperiment?

Using `XcmsExperiment` as the central input and output object provides several
advantages.

Avoids duplicating LC-MS preprocessing functionality: Earlier versions of LipidMS implemented the complete LC-MS workflow because xcms did not yet provide all the functionality required to handle simultaneously full scna, DDA and DIA data. With the recent updates of xcms capabilities, these preprocessing steps can now be delegated to the xcms framework, avoiding redundant implementations while benefiting from its more efficient peak detection, retention-time alignment, feature correspondence, and data handling in terms of computation time and memory usage.

Native Bioconductor integration: enables seamless connection of lipid annotation with other Bioconductor packages for QC, statistical analysis, and data visualization. LipidMS results can be directly incorporated into established workflows for differential analysis, functional and pathway enrichment, and multi-omics integration. This provides a unified and reproducible environment from LC-MS data processing and lipid annotation to downstream statistical analysis and biological interpretation.

Modular and extensible architecture: preprocessing and lipid annotation become independent components that can evolve separately.

Scalability: LipidMS benefits from xcms data structures and BiocParallel-compatible workflows for large LC-MS datasets.

# Summary

A complete LipidMS analysis can therefore be represented as:

```text
mzML files
    |
    v
readMsExperiment()
    |
    v
findChromPeaks()
    |
    v
groupChromPeaks()
    |
    v
adjustRtime()
    |
    v
XcmsExperiment
    |
    v
annotateLipids()
    |
    v
Annotated XcmsExperiment
    |
    +--> chromPeakData()
    |
    +--> featureDefinitions()
    |
    +--> featureValues()
```

The main advantage of this approach is that lipid annotation becomes part of
the same Bioconductor object used for chromatographic processing and
quantification, reducing the need for intermediate files and preserving the
relationship between spectra, chromatographic peaks, features and lipid
annotations.
